grh_13146d4d56f1d606b245.title: Thelma Jordan
paragraphs: Assistant district attorney Cleve Marshall, unhappy at home and drinking after hours, meets the mysterious Thelma Jordan when she comes to the district attorneyâ€™s office about supposed break-ins at the home of her wealthy aunt Vera. Cleve begins an affair with her, unaware that Thelma and her lover Tony Laredo have been planning to rob Vera. When Vera catches Thelma at the safe, Thelma shoots her and then calls Cleve, who becomes trapped into destroying evidence and helping construct her alibi. Cleve later prosecutes the very case he has compromised, and Thelma is acquitted. After the trial Tony returns to claim Thelma and her inheritance, while Cleve finally forces the truth into the open. Thelma admits killing Vera and admits Cleve was meant to be the useful man inside the law, but she also reveals that her feelings for him became real. She leaves with Tony, deliberately drives their car into a crash, and gives a final confession that protects Cleve from being exposed as her Mr. X. Cleve loses his law career, but survives with the possibility of repairing his life with his wife Pamela.

This [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]] broadcast aired on March 15, 1951. It is listed as episode 94 in the archive. [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Wendell Corey, Barbara Stanwyck, [[person|william-conrad|William Conrad]], Hy Averback, and Stan Waxman. Other credited names include Bill Cairn as director, Howard Wiley as producer, Marty Howland as writer, Jack Rubin as radio adaptor, and Jimmy Wallington as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 60 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.0ee8343bca2245d4|Chesterfield]] and [[org|org.47c43e9eb0213c63|RCA]].
This version presents a radio version of [[work|work.sdp.film.4430322a29a9b269|Thelma Jordan]]. Jack Rubin adapted it for radio.

grh_132f04d2c76024040870.title: Forbidden Hill
paragraphs: Fourteen years after seven schoolchildren died from poison placed in a well at Cedar Hill, Margaret Anderson returns to Riverâ€™s End with her brother Roderick, the man who was blamed for the crime and committed to an asylum. Dr. Christian has always doubted that Roderick was insane, but the town still remembers him as a killer. Margaret repeatedly calls the doctor to the decaying house, while Roderick angrily tries to keep him away and appears to be threatening his sister. During a later visit Margaret serves Dr. Christian and Judy poisoned tea, but Roderick bursts in and knocks it from their hands, apparently attacking them. Laboratory testing confirms the poison and reverses the apparent roles. Dr. Christian concludes that Margaret, not Roderick, poisoned the children years earlier and is still dangerously disturbed. Roderick had understood his sisterâ€™s condition and silently accepted suspicion and confinement rather than expose her. His violent-looking intervention at Cedar Hill was actually another attempt to protect innocent people from her, finally giving Dr. Christian the proof needed to clear the man he never believed was insane.

The cast includes Jean Hersholt and Rosemary De Camp. Other credited names include Art Gilmore as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 23 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_13abca4b363e52f23ee8.title: Yellow Sky
paragraphs: After a bank robbery, outlaw leader Stretch and his exhausted gang cross a deadly desert and reach the abandoned mining town of Yellow Sky. There they find only an old prospector and his fiercely independent granddaughter Mike, who are secretly working a rich gold claim. The gang quickly turns on its hosts and on itself over the treasure, while Stretch, increasingly drawn to Mike, tries to keep the others from simply taking everything. Greed splits the outlaws into rival factions, and Dude and Lengthy move to seize the gold for themselves. Stretch survives the final gunfight, returns his gun to Mike, and declares that he is through with the life that brought him there. With the dangerous members of the gang gone, he asks Mike and her grandfather to let him remain in Yellow Sky.

grh_13f87075e81b633051e9.title: Back To Youth
paragraphs: Forty-two-year-old Kent Lewis has lost his clothing business, cannot find work and has begun to believe everyone who tells him he is already old and finished. Dr. Christian pairs him with energetic seventy-year-old Grandma Nelson, whose appetite for hiking, exploring and adventure makes Kent feel young again and restores the confidence his business failure destroyed. Grandma's worried grandson Ted accuses the doctor of pushing her too hard, but she insists that age is largely a state of mind. The lesson becomes more complicated when Grandma returns alone to an abandoned house she wants to explore, falls asleep after lighting a fire and must be rescued when the house catches fire. Kent proves he is far from finished by helping save her, while Grandma admits that feeling young does not mean ignoring every physical limit.
